external_source: AirPassengers — Box & Jenkins (1976) Series G, monthly international airline passengers 1949–1960; staged from statsforecast.utils.AirPassengersDF by scripts/stage_air_passengers.py (sha256 in the dataset's PROVENANCE.md)

cloud_recipe_1_2_0.note: best_model_mase identical to run b7f5853a (recipe 1.1.0) — reproducible

n_series.source: data function: the staged file has one series
n_series.note: Single series. The recipe must add a constant item id rather than invent several.

prediction_length.source: the recipe's own rule (~10% of median series length, min 1) applied to 144 observations; reference.py horizon()
prediction_length.note: Deliberately NOT the conventional 12: the recipe derives its horizon and forbids hardcoding it, and the reference uses the same 14-month holdout so the MASE figures are comparable.

best_model_mase.source: reference.py: seasonal-naive holdout MASE on the same 14-month window (1959-11 … 1960-12), m=12
best_model_mase.tol_basis: Threshold, not a target value: the run must beat seasonal-naive on the identical holdout. Quality beyond the floor is graded against the reference block (see notes.md), not pass/fail.
best_model_mase.note: The floor is seasonal-naive's own holdout MASE (1.94), NOT 1.0. MASE divides by the in-sample seasonal-naive error, and on a trending series seasonal-naive falls further behind every year, so it scores well above 1 out of sample. 'MASE < 1 = beats seasonal-naive' only holds in-sample.

seasonal_naive_mase.source: reference.py seasonal_naive (equals AutoGluon's SeasonalNaive score_val on the same window: 1.941386 on run b7f5853a)
seasonal_naive_mase.note: Recipe >= 1.2.0 reports the baseline it compares against. Checking it catches a run that compares against the wrong yardstick. Run b7f5853a used recipe 1.1.0, which did not emit it.

quality_bands.note: Not pass criteria. Grade a passing run by its best_model_mase relative to the analytic reference block below (same window, same scale).
quality_bands.adequate: 0.40 – 1.27  — between the best classical models and AutoETS
quality_bands.weak: 1.27 – 1.94  — worse than AutoETS, but beats seasonal-naive
